subject: OpenCR survivorship and population trends spatial vs non-spatial

messages.author: 7329857f6e47dae0
messages.subject: OpenCR survivorship and population trends spatial vs non-spatial
parts:
Hello,

I've been using OpenCR for a little while and still learning about it. I've been exploring the same dataset with spatial and non spatial open pop models. 

I have derived apparent survival and pop trends from spatial and non spatial open CR models and i get very different results. So i'm trying to understand why this is. I'm also wondering whether it is standard practice to present density numbers and calculate pop trends and apparent survival with non-spatial model. 

The table below summarises my capture data:

Survival calculated under a non spatial simple model (phi~t, p~1) produces the following results:


While deriving the same parameter with the spatial version (type= "CJSsecr", model= list(phi~t, lambda0~t, )) produces the following plot, which suggests that all the animals from 2017 survived to 2018, which is not correct (albeit confidence intervals for that data point are all wonky).





 Regarding population trends. The non-spatial model suggesting a sharp decline between 2016-2017 (lambda = 0.03), while for the same interval the spatial model produces a value of 0.8. If i well don't expect to get the same answer from both methods, i would think that i should be expecting the same patterns and 0.03 is sharply different from 0.8.

Any insights would be greatly appreciated. 


Diana

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: OpenCR survivorship and population trends spatial vs non-spatial
parts:
Diana
Getting sense from CJSsecr requires that you set details = list(CJSp1 = TRUE). Did you do that? This peculiarity is (hidden?) in a footnote on p3 of the vignette, and explained in Section 7.2 and Appendix E of Efford & Schofield (2020).
Also, to estimate population trend you need to fit a model with recruitment at least a PLBsecrX (=JSSAsecrXCL) model, where X is f, l, etc. Are you confusing lambda (population trend) and lambda0 (detection intercept)? It would help to see your actual code.
Murray
